prerequisites: Basic knowledge of computer science and electronics

learning_outcomes.text: Upon completion of the course, students will be able to understand the fundamental principles of electronic measurements, experimental data acquisition and processing methodologies, the characteristics of electronic measurement instruments, and the main signal processing techniques. Students will also understand the concepts of measurement uncertainty and the main sources of error in measurement processes.

Students will be able to apply the acquired knowledge to perform measurements using digital electronic instrumentation, acquire and process signals, analyze experimental data, and evaluate the uncertainty associated with measurement results. They will also be able to use appropriate methods and tools to address basic measurement problems in engineering applications.

Students will be able to critically evaluate measurement results, interpret experimental data, identify the main sources of error, and assess the reliability of the obtained results. They will also be able to select the most appropriate measurement methods and instruments according to the specific problem under consideration.

Students will be able to clearly and rigorously communicate the adopted methodologies, experimental results, and related analyses using appropriate technical and scientific terminology. They will also be able to present and discuss measurement results through graphs, tables, and technical reports.

Students will develop the ability to independently expand their knowledge in the field of electronic measurements, understand the operation of new measurement instruments and techniques, and continuously update their skills in response to technological developments in data acquisition and signal processing.

syllabus_topics: Statistic methods for the analysis of experimental data
Analogue electronic instrumentation (voltmeters, ammeters, multimeters, counters)
Digital electronic instrumentation (voltmeters, ammeters, multimeters, counters)

assessment_methods.method: Oral interview (2 questions related to the course syllabus)

assessment_rules: The final exam consists of an oral interview designed to assess knowledge of the topics covered in the program and the knowledge developed in the laboratory activities. The following are assessed: relevance of answers, quality of content, mastery of technical language, ability to connect topics, and ability to provide examples. Laboratory activities account for 33% of the overall grade, and 2 questions related to the course syllabus account for 66% of the overall grade.
